text: Regulation No. 07-01 of 09/01/2007 — Regulation No. 07-01 of 09/01/2007, relating to the rules applicable to current transactions with abroad and foreign currency accounts, amended and replaced Regulation No. 91-12 relating to the bank domiciliation of imports, Regulation No. 91-13 relating to the domiciliation of non-hydrocarbon exports, and Regulation No. 95-07 relating to exchange control.
heading_path: Regulation No. 07-01 of 09/01/2007

text: Regulation No. 07-01 of 09/01/2007 — The purpose of this regulation is to define the principle of convertibility of the national currency for current international transactions and the rules applicable to transfers to and from abroad related to these transactions, as well as the rights and obligations of foreign trade operators and authorized intermediaries in this matter.
heading_path: Regulation No. 07-01 of 09/01/2007

text: Regulation No. 07-01 of 09/01/2007 — The present document is intended to comment on the new measures introduced by this new regulation, the application of which falls directly on the customs administration.
heading_path: Regulation No. 07-01 of 09/01/2007
Regulation No. 07-01 of 09/01/2007 > 6 - Operations carried out by travelers > 6-1 Import and export of means of payment

text:
Regulation No. 07-01 of 09/01/2007 > 6 - Operations carried out by travelers > 6-2 Import of means of payment (Article 19) — Within the meaning of Article 19, any traveler entering Algeria is authorized to import foreign banknotes and traveler's checks, subject to a customs declaration for any amount exceeding a threshold set by instruction of the Bank of Algeria.

To this end, and pending the publication of the instruction setting the threshold from which the traveler must submit a currency declaration, the service must require entering travelers to the national territory to submit the said declaration.
heading_path: Regulation No. 07-01 of 09/01/2007 > 6 - Operations carried out by travelers > 6-2 Import of means of payment (Article 19)
Regulation No. 07-01 of 09/01/2007 > 6 - Operations carried out by travelers > 6-3 Export of means of payment (Article 20)

text:
Regulation No. 07-01 of 09/01/2007 > 6 - Operations carried out by travelers > 6-4 Import and export of national currency — Article 6 of the regulation introduced a new measure allowing travelers to import and export fiduciary currency in dinars, within the limit of a threshold to be set by instruction of the Bank of Algeria. Also, pending the setting of this threshold, our services must prohibit any import or export of Dinars.

Such are the clarifications deemed useful to communicate to you. Any difficulties encountered in the application of this regulation must be reported to me under this stamp.
heading_path: Regulation No. 07-01 of 09/01/2007 > 6 - Operations carried out by travelers > 6-4 Import and export of national currency
Regulation No. 07-01 of 09/01/2007 > 1 - General principles > 1-1 Notion of resident

text:
Regulation No. 07-01 of 09/01/2007 > 1 - General principles > 1-3 Import and export of securities denominated in national currency — In accordance with Article 6, the import or export of any debt security, movable security or means of payment denominated in national currency is prohibited, except with the authorization of the Bank of Algeria.

Also, it is up to your services, during the control of travelers, to ensure that securities, in particular shares and bonds issued by public or private companies, Treasury Bonds and Cash Bonds, may only be imported or exported under cover of an authorization from the Bank of Algeria.
heading_path: Regulation No. 07-01 of 09/01/2007 > 1 - General principles > 1-3 Import and export of securities denominated in national currency

text: Règlement N°07-01 du 09/01/2007 — Le règlement N°07-01 du 09/01/2007, relatif aux règles applicables aux transactions courantes avec l'étranger et aux comptes devises a modifié et remplacé les règlements n°91-12 relatif à la domiciliation bancaire des importations, le règlement n°91-13, relatif à la domiciliation des exportations hors hydrocarbures et le règlement n°95-07 relatif au contrôle des changes.
heading_path: Règlement N°07-01 du 09/01/2007

text: Règlement N°07-01 du 09/01/2007 — Ce règlement a pour objet de définir le principe de la convertibilité de la monnaie nationale pour les transactions internationales courantes et les règles applicables en matière de transferts de et vers l'étranger liées à ces transactions, ainsi que les droits et les obligations des opérateurs du commerce extérieur et des intermédiaires agréés en la matière.
heading_path: Règlement N°07-01 du 09/01/2007

text: Règlement N°07-01 du 09/01/2007 — La présente a pour objet de commenter les nouvelles mesures introduites par ce nouveau règlement et dont l'application incombe directement à l'administration des douanes.
heading_path: Règlement N°07-01 du 09/01/2007
Règlement N°07-01 du 09/01/2007 > 6 - Les opérations réalisées par les voyageurs > 6-1 Importation et exportation des moyens de paiement

text: Règlement N°07-01 du 09/01/2007 > 6 - Les opérations réalisées par les voyageurs > 6-2 Importation de moyens de paiement (Article 19) — Au sens de l'article 19 tous voyageurs entrant en Algérie est autorisé à importer des billets de banque étrangers et des chèques de voyage, sous réserve d'une déclaration en douane pour tout montant supérieur à un seuil fixé, par instruction de la banque d'Algérie.
heading_path: Règlement N°07-01 du 09/01/2007 > 6 - Les opérations réalisées par les voyageurs > 6-2 Importation de moyens de paiement (Article 19)

text: Règlement N°07-01 du 09/01/2007 > 6 - Les opérations réalisées par les voyageurs > 6-2 Importation de moyens de paiement (Article 19) — A ce titre, et en attendant la parution de l'instruction fixant le seuil à partir duquel le voyageur doit souscrire une déclaration devise, le service devra exiger des voyageurs entrant sur le territoire national la souscription de la dite déclaration.
heading_path: Règlement N°07-01 du 09/01/2007 > 6 - Les opérations réalisées par les voyageurs > 6-2 Importation de moyens de paiement (Article 19)
Règlement N°07-01 du 09/01/2007 > 6 - Les opérations réalisées par les voyageurs > 6-3 Exportation de moyens de paiement (Article 20)

text: Règlement N°07-01 du 09/01/2007 > 6 - Les opérations réalisées par les voyageurs > 6-4 Importation et exportation de la monnaie nationale — L'article 6 du règlement a introduit une nouvelle mesure permettant aux voyageurs d'importer et d'exporter de la monnaie fiduciaire en dinars, dans la limite d'un seuil qui sera fixé par instruction de la banque d'Algérie. Aussi, en attendant la fixation de ce seuil, nos services devront interdire toute importation ou exportation de Dinars.
heading_path: Règlement N°07-01 du 09/01/2007 > 6 - Les opérations réalisées par les voyageurs > 6-4 Importation et exportation de la monnaie nationale

text: Règlement N°07-01 du 09/01/2007 > 6 - Les opérations réalisées par les voyageurs > 6-4 Importation et exportation de la monnaie nationale — Telles sont les précisions jugées utiles à vous communiquer. Toutes difficultés rencontrées dans l'application de ce règlement devront m'être signalées sous le présent timbre.
heading_path: Règlement N°07-01 du 09/01/2007 > 6 - Les opérations réalisées par les voyageurs > 6-4 Importation et exportation de la monnaie nationale
Règlement N°07-01 du 09/01/2007 > 1 - Principes généraux > 1-1 Notion de résident

text: Règlement N°07-01 du 09/01/2007 > 1 - Principes généraux > 1-3 Importation et exportation de valeurs libellées en monnaie nationale — Conformément à l'article 6, l'importation ou l'exportation de tout titre de créance, valeur mobilière ou moyen de paiement libellé en monnaie nationale est interdite, sauf autorisation de la banque d'Algérie.
heading_path: Règlement N°07-01 du 09/01/2007 > 1 - Principes généraux > 1-3 Importation et exportation de valeurs libellées en monnaie nationale

text: Règlement N°07-01 du 09/01/2007 > 1 - Principes généraux > 1-3 Importation et exportation de valeurs libellées en monnaie nationale — Aussi, il appartient à vos services, lors du contrôle des voyageurs, de veiller à ce que les titres, notamment, les actions et les obligations émises par les entreprises publiques ou privées, les Bons de trésor et les Bons de caisse, ne puissent être importés ou exportés que sous couvert d'une autorisation de la banque d'Algérie.
heading_path: Règlement N°07-01 du 09/01/2007 > 1 - Principes généraux > 1-3 Importation et exportation de valeurs libellées en monnaie nationale
Personal items and effects imported by travelers

text:
Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Temporarily imported personal items and effects — Travelers (foreigners or non-resident nationals) who come to stay temporarily in the customs territory can temporarily import, upon request and after submitting a simplified declaration with a commitment to re-export exempt from deposit, all new or used items intended for their personal use, as listed by regulatory means.

Duration of temporary importation:

The duration of temporary importation of personal items and effects by travelers is set to:
heading_path: Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Temporarily imported personal items and effects

text:
Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Temporarily imported personal items and effects — For non-resident nationals:
- Six (06) months non-extendable.

For non-resident foreigners:
- Three (03) months extendable.

Upon the expiration of the granted deadlines, the items must be re-exported, abandoned to the Treasury, or put to use under the conditions set forth by current legislation and regulations.
heading_path: Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Temporarily imported personal items and effects

text:
Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Items and effects admitted duty and tax-free — Travelers can import items intended for their personal or family use, duty and tax-free, provided that the value does not exceed 150,000.00 DA.

These items must not, by their nature, quantity, or value, raise concerns of a commercial or professional nature.

Travelers are not authorized to import goods of a commercial nature, particularly mobile phones, whose importation is subject to specific regulations.
heading_path: Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Items and effects admitted duty and tax-free
Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Items and effects admitted to flat-rate taxation > Personal use items

text:
Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Items and effects admitted to flat-rate taxation > Personal use items — The customs clearance of these goods results in a flat-rate tax of 30% of the value of the goods, determined according to Article 16 and subsequent articles of the customs code.

Importation of mobile phones and computer equipment for personal or family use:

Mobile phones and computer equipment for personal or family use are exempt from the aforementioned flat-rate tax.
heading_path: Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Items and effects admitted to flat-rate taxation > Personal use items

text:
Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Items and effects admitted to flat-rate taxation > Professional use items — Travelers can clear through customs, without the formalities of foreign trade and currency exchange, new or used goods imported for professional use, provided they are not intended for commercial sale as-is and their value does not exceed one hundred thousand dinars (100,000 DA).

This customs clearance incurs a flat-rate tax of 25% of the value of the goods, determined according to Article 16 and subsequent articles of the customs code.
heading_path: Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Items and effects admitted to flat-rate taxation > Professional use items

text:
Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Items and effects admitted to flat-rate taxation > Professional use items — Goods whose value exceeds the flat-rate tax threshold must be subject to an authorized regime or destination.

Note: Start-ups are exempt from paying the flat-rate tax in this context.
heading_path: Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Items and effects admitted to flat-rate taxation > Professional use items

text:
Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Duty-free allowances (Tobacco, wine, spirits, and perfumes) — Regarding tobacco, wine, spirits, and perfumes, the following quantities can be imported duty-free by travelers:
- Tobacco: 200 cigarettes or 50 cigars or a combination of these products up to 250 grams;
- Alcohol: two (2) liters of wine or one (1) liter of spirits.
- Perfumes: 50 grams of perfume and 1/4 liter of eau de toilette.
heading_path: Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Duty-free allowances (Tobacco, wine, spirits, and perfumes)

text:
Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Declaration by the traveler — Travelers are allowed to make a verbal declaration for the goods accompanying them.

However, customs may require a written declaration for goods carried by travelers when they are imported as part of the exercise of their business activity, after meeting the legal and regulatory conditions in force.
heading_path: Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Declaration by the traveler

text: Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Sensitive equipment — Travelers are not permitted to import sensitive equipment such as drones, binoculars, GPS devices, weapons, and their accessories, as their importation is subject to specific regulations.
heading_path: Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Sensitive equipment
Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Pets

text: Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Traveler control — In addition to the control of travelers carried out during the completion of regulatory formalities.
heading_path: Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Traveler control
Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Traveler control
Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Traveler control

text:
Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Traveler control — The storage period for goods placed in customs by travelers is set at one (01) month.

Upon expiration of this period, the goods are sold by the customs administration.
heading_path: Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Traveler control

text:
Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Export of personal items > Export under temporary exemption — Travelers (foreign or national residents) who will temporarily stay outside the customs territory may temporarily export items exclusively for their personal or family use, excluding goods prohibited for export absolutely.

Also excluded are goods that, by their nature and quantity, raise commercial or professional concerns.
heading_path: Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Export of personal items > Export under temporary exemption

text:
Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Export of personal items > Temporary export — Travelers (foreign or national residents) who will temporarily stay outside the customs territory may export items duty-free, upon request and after submitting a simplified declaration with a commitment to re-import without a bond, all new or used items intended for their personal use.

The duration of duty-free temporary export of items is set at six (06) months.

Items temporarily exported must be re-imported for the clearance of commitments made.
heading_path: Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Export of personal items > Temporary export

text:
Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Abandoned in favor of the Public Treasury — Objects temporarily imported by travelers must be re-exported.

These objects may be abandoned to the Public Treasury, with the authorized customs receiver.

N.B:
- Abandonment is an act falling within the exclusive prerogatives of the customs receiver;
- Before any acceptance, the customs receiver must decide on the appropriateness of abandonment, considering the condition of the object.
heading_path: Personal items and effects imported by travelers > Abandoned in favor of the Public Treasury
Currency Declaration > Legal and regulatory basis

text: Currency Declaration > Legal and regulatory basis — - Ordinance 96-22 of 09/07/1996 relating to the repression of offenses against the legislation and regulations on exchange and capital movements to and from abroad, as amended and supplemented by Ordinance No. 03-01 of 19/02/2003 and by Ordinance No. 10-03 of 26/08/2010 (Articles 1, 1 bis and 2);
heading_path: Currency Declaration > Legal and regulatory basis

text: Currency Declaration > Legal and regulatory basis — - Executive Decree No. 12-279 of 09 July 2012, setting the terms of organization and operation of the national file of offenders in matters of offenses against the legislation and regulations on exchange and capital movements to and from abroad (Articles 2, 3, 4 and 5);
heading_path: Currency Declaration > Legal and regulatory basis

text:
Currency Declaration > Legal and regulatory basis — - Bank of Algeria Regulation No. 16-02 of 21/04/2016 setting the declaration threshold for the import and export of banknotes and/or negotiable instruments denominated in freely convertible foreign currencies, by residents and non-residents;

- Instruction No. 04-2016 of 1 September 2016 relating to the export and import of Algerian banknotes.
heading_path: Currency Declaration > Legal and regulatory basis
Currency Declaration > Legal and regulatory basis
Currency Declaration > Legal and regulatory basis

text: Currency Declaration > 2 - On entry into the national territory — Any traveler is authorized to import currency without any limit on amount, subject to satisfying the declaration obligation with the customs services.
heading_path: Currency Declaration > 2 - On entry into the national territory
Currency Declaration > 3 - On exit from the national territory

text:
Currency Declaration > 3 - On exit from the national territory — - banknotes, coins, bearer payment instruments, commercial paper, securities and other negotiable and transferable instruments.

Non-resident travelers are required to present a bank receipt attesting to the exchange of part or all of the currencies (exceeding 1,000 euros) declared upon entry into the national territory.
heading_path: Currency Declaration > 3 - On exit from the national territory

text:
Currency Declaration > 4 - Declaration procedure — The currency declaration may be made:

- electronically, before arrival at the customs office;
- in writing, on entry or exit from the national territory, in accordance with the regulatory forms.

Declaration forms are available at customs offices.

The declaration form is also downloadable from the official website of the General Directorate of Customs.
heading_path: Currency Declaration > 4 - Declaration procedure

text: Currency Declaration > 4 - Declaration procedure > Entry and exit of the Algerian dinar — Any resident traveler is authorized to import and export Algerian banknotes up to the limit of 10,000 Algerian dinars (10,000 DA).
heading_path: Currency Declaration > 4 - Declaration procedure > Entry and exit of the Algerian dinar

text:
Currency Declaration > VERY IMPORTANT — - The declaration of currency, precious metals and precious stones is mandatory, as is that of coins, bearer payment instruments, commercial paper, securities and other negotiable instruments.

- The declaration is primarily submitted electronically before arrival at the customs office.

- It may also be made in writing in accordance with the regulatory forms.

- The declaration form is valid for a single stay only.
heading_path: Currency Declaration > VERY IMPORTANT

text:
Currency Declaration > VERY IMPORTANT — - Any declared amount must be presented to customs officers for control purposes.

- The shipment of foreign currency banknotes, coins or any bearer payment instrument by freight or mail is prohibited.

- The declaration must be made before crossing the limits of the places designated for customs control.

- Import and export operations of precious metals and precious stones are subject to the legislative and regulatory provisions in force.
heading_path: Currency Declaration > VERY IMPORTANT
La Déclaration de la monnaie > Base légale et réglementaire

text: La Déclaration de la monnaie > Base légale et réglementaire — - Ordonnance 96-22 du 09/07/1996 relative à la répression de l'infraction à la législation et à la réglementation des changes et des mouvements de capitaux de et vers l'étranger, modifiée et complétée par l'ordonnance n°03-01 du 19/02/2003 et par l'ordonnance n°10-03 du 26/08/2010 (articles 1, 1 bis et 2);
heading_path: La Déclaration de la monnaie > Base légale et réglementaire

text: La Déclaration de la monnaie > Base légale et réglementaire — - Décret exécutif n°12-279 du 09 juillet 2012, fixant les modalités d'organisation et de fonctionnement du fichier national des contrevenants en matière d'infraction à la législation et à la réglementation des changes et des mouvements des capitaux de et vers l'étranger (articles 2, 3, 4 et 5)
heading_path: La Déclaration de la monnaie > Base légale et réglementaire

text:
La Déclaration de la monnaie > Base légale et réglementaire — - Règlement de la Banque d'Algérie n°16-02 du 21/04/2016 fixant le seuil de déclaration d'importation et d'exportation de billets de banques et/ou instruments négociables libellés en monnaies étrangères librement convertibles, par les résidents et les non-résidents;

- Instruction n°04-2016 du 1er septembre 2016 relative à l'exportation et l'importation de billets de banque algériens.
heading_path: La Déclaration de la monnaie > Base légale et réglementaire
La Déclaration de la monnaie > Base légale et réglementaire
La Déclaration de la monnaie > Base légale et réglementaire

text: La Déclaration de la monnaie > 2- A l'entrée du territoire national — Tout voyageur est autorisé à importer de la monnaie sans limitation de montant, sous réserve de satisfaire à l'obligation de déclaration auprès des services des douanes.
heading_path: La Déclaration de la monnaie > 2- A l'entrée du territoire national
La Déclaration de la monnaie > 3- A la sortie du territoire national
La Déclaration de la monnaie > 3- A la sortie du territoire national

text:
La Déclaration de la monnaie > 4- Procédure de déclaration — La déclaration de la monnaie peut être effectuée:

- par voie électronique, avant l'arrivée au bureau des douanes;
- par écrit, à l'entrée ou à la sortie du territoire national, conformément aux formulaires réglementaires.

Les formulaires de déclaration sont disponibles auprès des bureaux de douane.

Le formulaire de déclaration est également téléchargeable sur le site officiel de la Direction Générale des Douanes.
heading_path: La Déclaration de la monnaie > 4- Procédure de déclaration

text: La Déclaration de la monnaie > 4- Procédure de déclaration > Entrée et sortie du dinar algérien — Tout voyageur résident est autorisé à importer et à exporter des billets de banque algériens dans la limite de 10 000 dinars algériens (10 000 DA).
heading_path: La Déclaration de la monnaie > 4- Procédure de déclaration > Entrée et sortie du dinar algérien

text:
La Déclaration de la monnaie > TRÈS IMPORTANT — - La déclaration de la monnaie, des métaux précieux et des pierres précieuses est obligatoire, ainsi que celle des pièces de monnaie, des instruments de paiement au porteur, des effets de commerce, des valeurs et autres titres négociables.

- La déclaration est souscrite principalement par voie électronique avant l'arrivée au bureau des douanes.

- Elle peut également être effectuée par écrit conformément aux formulaires réglementaires.
heading_path: La Déclaration de la monnaie > TRÈS IMPORTANT

text:
La Déclaration de la monnaie > TRÈS IMPORTANT — - Le formulaire de déclaration n'est valable que pour un seul séjour.

- Tout montant déclaré doit être présenté aux agents des douanes à des fins de contrôle.

- L'expédition de billets de banque en monnaies étrangères, de pièces de monnaie ou de tout instrument de paiement au porteur par fret ou par courrier est interdite.

- La déclaration doit être effectuée avant le franchissement des limites des lieux désignés pour le contrôle douanier.
heading_path: La Déclaration de la monnaie > TRÈS IMPORTANT

text: La Déclaration de la monnaie > TRÈS IMPORTANT — - Les opérations d'importation et d'exportation des métaux précieux et des pierres précieuses sont soumises aux dispositions législatives et réglementaires en vigueur.
heading_path: La Déclaration de la monnaie > TRÈS IMPORTANT

text:
Consulate General of Algeria in London — Entry visa to Algeria > Visa terms — All non-Algerians need to apply for a visa to enter Algeria. There are exceptions for some nationals of foreign countries, listed below, who are exempted from visas:

All Nationals from: Libya, Malaysia, Maldives, Mali, Mauritania, Morocco, Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic, Seychelles, Tunisia.
heading_path: Consulate General of Algeria in London — Entry visa to Algeria > Visa terms
source_name: Consulate General of Algeria in London

text:
Consulate General of Algeria in London — Entry visa to Algeria > Visa terms — The Consulate General of Algeria in London will process visa applications made by **applicants residing in the UK only.** Others foreign citizens must provide "proof of residency in the UK". Regardless of their age, kids traveling with their parents need a visa.

British passport holders residing abroad must apply for their visa to Algeria at the Algerian Embassy or Consulate accredited in the country of their actual residence.
heading_path: Consulate General of Algeria in London — Entry visa to Algeria > Visa terms
source_name: Consulate General of Algeria in London

text:
Consulate General of Algeria in London — Entry visa to Algeria > Lodging of applications — Applicants must lodge their applications **in person or by couriers** at the Consulate General **between 9:30 am - 01:00 pm**, Tuesday to Saturday (no appointment needed). Visa applications can also be made **by post**.

Since working hours can be adjusted according to the Islamic holidays including Ramadan, please see Opening hours & holidays page for more details.

Applicants by post must send a **prepaid self-addressed special delivery envelope** for returning the passport(s).
heading_path: Consulate General of Algeria in London — Entry visa to Algeria > Lodging of applications
source_name: Consulate General of Algeria in London

text: Consulate General of Algeria in London — Entry visa to Algeria > Lodging of applications — **Note: any incomplete application, including the form, will be either rejected if lodged in person at the Consulate General or returned to the sender if made by post.**
heading_path: Consulate General of Algeria in London — Entry visa to Algeria > Lodging of applications
source_name: Consulate General of Algeria in London

text: Consulate General of Algeria in London — Entry visa to Algeria > Processing time — The processing time may vary according to the nationality of the applicant and the visa type. However, visas submitted in person are generally issued within **10 working days**. For the applications sent by post, the processing time is **at least 15 working days**.
heading_path: Consulate General of Algeria in London — Entry visa to Algeria > Processing time
source_name: Consulate General of Algeria in London

text:
Consulate General of Algeria in London — Entry visa to Algeria > Processing time — During certain periods of the year (summer holidays, New Year's holidays, Ramadhan, Eid celebrations), the processing time may be extended by 5 more working days for each period indicated above. This is due to the high volume of applications being processed.

The processing of an application may be delayed if prior agreement by Algerian authorities is required.

The Consulate General reserves the right to request additional documentation from applicants.
heading_path: Consulate General of Algeria in London — Entry visa to Algeria > Processing time
source_name: Consulate General of Algeria in London

text:
Consulate General of Algeria in London — Entry visa to Algeria > Processing time — The Consulate General has **no express service** to process applications merely due to planned travel date, the Consulate General advise also not to buy non-refundable or non-flexible ticket until the visa is issued.

The responsibility for any financial loss occurred lies with the applicant(s).

The date of departure does not affect the processing time of the visa.

For applications sent by post, the processing time starts only when the application is received by our office.
heading_path: Consulate General of Algeria in London — Entry visa to Algeria > Processing time
source_name: Consulate General of Algeria in London

text: Consulate General of Algeria in London — Entry visa to Algeria > Processing time — The Consulate General is not responsible for delays due to postal services. Please take note of the code bar number of your recorded envelope to be able to track your returned mail.
heading_path: Consulate General of Algeria in London — Entry visa to Algeria > Processing time
source_name: Consulate General of Algeria in London

text:
Consulate General of Algeria in London — Entry visa to Algeria > Return of passports — Applicants may pick up their passports at the Consulate General between 9:30 am - 1:00 pm Tuesday to Saturday (please see Opening hours & holidays page for more details) or send a "prepaid self-addressed special delivery envelope".

The Consulate General is not responsible for the loss or delays of documents by the post office or other visa services.
heading_path: Consulate General of Algeria in London — Entry visa to Algeria > Return of passports
source_name: Consulate General of Algeria in London

text:
Consulate General of Algeria in London — Entry visa to Algeria > Travel insurance — Travel insurance is not required for British and Irish citizens.

The travel insurance is mandatory for the citizens of the following countries:

Australia, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, F.Y.R. of Macedonia, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands (The), New Zealand, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Romania.
heading_path: Consulate General of Algeria in London — Entry visa to Algeria > Travel insurance
source_name: Consulate General of Algeria in London

text: Consulate General of Algeria in London — Entry visa to Algeria > Travel insurance — The day of insurance is the first day of validity of the visa.
heading_path: Consulate General of Algeria in London — Entry visa to Algeria > Travel insurance
source_name: Consulate General of Algeria in London

text: Embassy of Algeria in Beijing — Entry visa to Algeria — **Very important note: The Embassy does not accept visa application documents received through any form of post mail. These documents must be submitted by THE APPLICANT HIMSELF to the visa Office at the Embassy of Algeria in Beijing, without any intermediaries.**
heading_path: Embassy of Algeria in Beijing — Entry visa to Algeria

text:
Embassy of Algeria in Beijing — Entry visa to Algeria > 1. All applicants residing in the People's Republic of China who wish to travel to Algeria may need a visa issued by the Visa section of the Embassy of Algeria in Beijing. > IMPORTANT INFORMATIONS — - Visa applications are accepted from Monday to Wednesday, from 9:30 AM to 11:00 AM.

- The visa can be withdrawn from Monday to Friday (from 9:30 AM to 11:00 AM).

- **The application for the visa must be deposited by the applicant himself.**

- The Embassy issues single entry visa, two entry visa and multiple entry visa.

text:
Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice — This information is for people travelling on a full 'British citizen' passport from the UK. It is based on the UK government's understanding of Algeria's current rules for the most common types of travel.

The authorities in Algeria set and enforce entry rules. If you're not sure how these requirements apply to you, contact the Algerian Consulate in the UK.
heading_path: Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice

text:
Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice > Passport validity requirements — To enter Algeria, your passport must have an 'expiry date' at least 6 months after the date you arrive.

Check with your travel provider that your passport and other travel documents meet requirements. Renew your passport if you need to.

You will be denied entry if you do not have a valid travel document or try to use a passport that has been reported lost or stolen.
heading_path: Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice > Passport validity requirements

text: Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice > Dual nationals — When returning to the UK, British citizens must carry a valid British passport or certificate of entitlement. See Dual Citizenship.
heading_path: Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice > Dual nationals

text: Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice > Dual nationals > If your passport is lost or stolen in Algeria — If your passport is lost or stolen during your stay, the Algerian authorities will ask for a police report when you leave the country.
heading_path: Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice > Dual nationals > If your passport is lost or stolen in Algeria

text:
Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice > Visa requirements — You must have a visa to visit Algeria.

Check your visa details, including validity dates, before you travel. If you overstay, it is likely Algerian immigration police will detain you at the airport on departure. You may face criminal prosecution and up to 3 months in prison.

If you want to extend your stay in Algeria, apply at the town hall ('la wilaya') nearest to you.
heading_path: Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice > Visa requirements

text:
Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice > Visa requirements > Applying for a visa — Before you travel, apply for a visa through the Algerian Consulate in the UK.

You may be able to get a tourist visa on arrival at some airports in Algeria if the majority of your travel is in the south of the country. You should have a confirmed reservation with an approved local travel agency. Contact the Algerian Consulate in the UK for more information and for details of approved travel agencies.
heading_path: Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice > Visa requirements > Applying for a visa

text:
Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice > Vaccine requirements — To enter Algeria, you must have a certificate to prove you've had a yellow fever vaccination if you're coming from a country listed as a transmission risk.

For full details about medical entry requirements and recommended vaccinations, see TravelHealthPro's Algeria guide.
heading_path: Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice > Vaccine requirements

text:
Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice > Travelling with children — In Algeria, a child is:

- someone under the age of 19 years and one day
- considered to be an Algerian citizen if one of their parents is Algerian

If an Algerian citizen or a British-Algerian dual national child travels with one parent, the parent (whether mother or father) must prove their parental link through a 'Livret de famille' (original or certified copy).
heading_path: Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice > Travelling with children

text:
Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice > Travelling with children — Algerian children travelling alone must have a letter ('Autorisation Parentale') from their parent or legal guardian giving them permission to leave the country. Children not from Algeria travelling alone need to show proof of permanent residence in the country they are travelling to.

For further information, check the website of the Algerian Ministry of Interior or contact the Algerian Consulate in London.
heading_path: Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice > Travelling with children

text: Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice > Customs rules — There are strict rules about goods you can take into and out of Algeria. You must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.
heading_path: Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice > Customs rules

text: Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice > Customs rules > Souvenirs — You can get a prison sentence for smuggling antiquities in Algeria. If you buy souvenirs, get proof of authenticity for anything that looks old or antique. Otherwise, the Algerian authorities may detain you on departure at the airport and confiscate the souvenirs.
heading_path: Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice > Customs rules > Souvenirs

text:
Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice > Customs rules > Taking money into and out of Algeria — Declare cash at your point of entry and exit into Algeria if the amount you are carrying exceeds 5000 euros or its equivalent in other currencies. Failure to declare or false declaration of imported and exported cash constitutes an offense which may lead to criminal prosecution.

Only travellers with residency status are allowed to bring in and take out Algerian banknotes, up to a maximum of 10,000 Algerian dinars.

For further details, see You arrive in Algeria - Direction Générale des Douanes.
heading_path: Entry requirements — Algeria travel advice > Customs rules > Taking money into and out of Algeria

text:
Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Terrorism — There is a high threat of terrorist attack globally affecting UK interests and British nationals, including from groups and individuals who view the UK and British nationals as targets. Stay aware of your surroundings at all times.

UK Counter Terrorism Policing has information and advice on staying safe and what to do in the event of a terrorist attack.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Terrorism

text:
Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Terrorism > Terrorism in Algeria — Terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Algeria.

Terrorist attacks could be indiscriminate, including in places visited by foreign nationals, such as:

- transport hubs
- locations popular with tourists and foreigners
- government buildings
- crowded places
- businesses with western interests

There is also a risk that lone actors target foreign nationals. Stay aware of your surroundings, keep up to date with local media reports and follow the advice of local authorities.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Terrorism > Terrorism in Algeria

text:
Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Terrorism > Terrorism in Algeria — The threat from terrorism is higher in some parts of the country, including:

- the southern border, where the kidnap risk is concentrated
- the Libyan and Tunisian borders
- rural, and in particular mountainous, areas in the north and between Tunisia and Algiers
- the Sahara
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Terrorism > Terrorism in Algeria

text:
Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Terrorism > Terrorism in Algeria — The terrorist threat comes from individuals inspired by Islamist extremist and anti-Semitic ideology and established groups, such as Al-Qaida in the Islamic Maghreb (AQIM). These groups have been active across the country and likely consider Western nationals legitimate targets.

The Algerian authorities conduct effective counter-terrorism operations and retain a strong, visible security presence across the country.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Terrorism > Terrorism in Algeria

text: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Terrorism > Terrorist kidnap — There is a threat of kidnapping by groups operating in North Africa, particularly from Libya, Mauritania and groups originating in the Sahel. This includes AQIM and Daesh-affiliated groups, who may travel across the region's porous border. There is a heightened risk of kidnap in border and remote desert areas of North Africa, particularly in the southern and eastern border areas (bordering Mali and Libya respectively).
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Terrorism > Terrorist kidnap

text:
Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Terrorism > Terrorist kidnap — Terrorist groups have kidnapped foreigners, government officials and civilians in the region for financial gain and for political leverage.

British nationals are seen as legitimate targets, including tourists, humanitarian aid workers, journalists and business travellers. If you are kidnapped, the reason for your presence is unlikely to protect you or secure your safe release.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Terrorism > Terrorist kidnap

text: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Terrorism > Terrorist kidnap — The long-standing policy of the British government is to not make substantive concessions to hostage takers. The British government considers that paying ransoms and releasing prisoners increases the risk of further hostage taking. The Terrorism Act (2000) also makes payments to terrorists illegal.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Terrorism > Terrorist kidnap

text: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Political situation — Algeria has a visible security presence across the country that gives considerable attention to the safety of its visitors. Demonstrations and other forms of protest are subject to various restrictions. You should take precautions for your personal safety by avoiding political gatherings and demonstrations. Follow instructions given by local security authorities.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Political situation

text: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Algeria-Morocco border — The land border between Algeria and Morocco is closed. Do not attempt to cross it.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Algeria-Morocco border

text:
Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Risk of arrest and detention — The Algerian authorities do not always inform the British Embassy when British nationals have been arrested. If you are detained, insist on your right to contact the British Embassy.

It can take time for the British Embassy to get the necessary permission to visit you.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Risk of arrest and detention

text:
Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Crime > Protecting yourself and your belongings — There is a risk of pickpocketing, robbery and petty theft in the larger cities in Algeria.

You can take precautions such as:

- avoiding areas that you do not know, especially after dark in the suburbs
- not carrying large amounts of money or valuables
- not accepting lifts from people you do not know – use a taxi service recommended by your hotel

Maintain at least the same level of personal security awareness as in the UK and take care when walking or travelling alone.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Crime > Protecting yourself and your belongings

text:
Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Crime > Protecting yourself and your belongings — If you plan to tour the Casbah area of Algiers, use a good local guide and make sure your hosts or hotel know your plans.

You should check the latest guidance of local authorities before moving around the country.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Crime > Protecting yourself and your belongings

text: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Crime > Security escorts — The Algerian authorities devote considerable resources to the safety of foreign visitors. There's a clear security presence, which can feel intrusive.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Crime > Security escorts

text: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Laws and cultural differences > Personal ID — You will need your passport to check in to any hotels in Algeria. You do not have to carry your passport at all times, but take it with you on longer journeys. You must have your passport if you travel inside Algeria by air. Keep copies of your passport's photo page and your visa or entry stamp in a separate place.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Laws and cultural differences > Personal ID

text:
Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Laws and cultural differences > Ramadan — Ramadan is a holy month for Muslims. The dates vary by year and country, next starting in February 2027. During this time, do not:

- eat, drink, smoke or chew gum in public in the daytime, including in your car
- play loud music or dance
- swear in public

Get more advice when you arrive from your tour guide, hotel or business contacts.

You should also:
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Laws and cultural differences > Ramadan

text:
Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Laws and cultural differences > Ramadan — - check opening hours of shops and restaurants
- be aware that if hotels and restaurants are providing food or drink in fasting hours, they may separate you from Islamic guests, for example with screens
- be aware that most restaurants do not serve alcohol
- follow local dress codes – clothing that does not meet local dress codes may cause more offence at this time
- be aware that fasting can cause tiredness, particularly during the later afternoon and early evening
- be patient and show tolerance
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Laws and cultural differences > Ramadan

text: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Laws and cultural differences > Alcohol laws — It is illegal to drink or be under the influence of alcohol in a public place.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Laws and cultural differences > Alcohol laws

text: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Laws and cultural differences > Illegal drugs and prison sentences — There is zero tolerance for drugs-related offences. The penalties for trafficking, smuggling, using and possessing illegal drugs are severe and can include the death penalty depending upon the severity of the offence.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Laws and cultural differences > Illegal drugs and prison sentences

text: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Laws and cultural differences > Mobile phone coverage — Mobile phone coverage can be patchy or unavailable in more remote areas, particularly in the south of Algeria. Some online maps may not be accurate in remote areas.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Laws and cultural differences > Mobile phone coverage

text: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Laws and cultural differences > Using cameras in secure areas — It is illegal to bring drones, binoculars, telescopes and certain types of photography equipment into Algeria without authorisation. If you have any doubt about items you plan to bring with you, contact the Algerian customs to check prior to your travel.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Laws and cultural differences > Using cameras in secure areas

text:
Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Laws and cultural differences > LGBT+ travellers — Sexual acts between people of the same sex are illegal in Algeria.

Read more advice for LGBT+ travellers.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Laws and cultural differences > LGBT+ travellers

text: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Laws and cultural differences > Family law and child custody — Algerian family law is different from UK law. Mothers cannot renew their children's passports without written consent from the father. Fathers can renew their children's passports without needing the mother's consent.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Laws and cultural differences > Family law and child custody

text: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Laws and cultural differences > Family law and child custody — Algerian nationals, including dual-nationals, who enter the country on an Algerian passport, must leave the country on an Algerian passport, so if you are travelling with a child who has British-Algerian dual nationality, and you are unable to access a valid Algerian passport for them, you will not be able to bring the child out of Algeria without the father's written consent or permission from the Algerian courts.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Laws and cultural differences > Family law and child custody

text: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Laws and cultural differences > Military service — If you are a British male of Algerian origin, you may be liable for national service even if you have been living outside of Algeria. You can contact the Algerian consulate near you to check your status prior to travelling to Algeria.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Laws and cultural differences > Military service

text:
Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Transport risks > Road travel — If you are planning to drive in Algeria, see information on driving abroad.

You can use a UK photocard driving licence to drive in Algeria for up to 3 months after you first arrive. If you still have a paper driving licence, you may need to update it to a photocard licence or get the correct version of the international driving permit (IDP) as well.

The Algerian authorities may ask to see an IDP. You cannot buy an IDP outside the UK, so get one before you travel.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Transport risks > Road travel

text: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Transport risks > Road travel — If you are planning to hire a car, check with your car hire company for information on their requirements before you travel.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Transport risks > Road travel

text:
Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Transport risks > Road conditions and safety — Algeria has a very high road traffic accident rate and driving can be erratic.

There is very little lane discipline and often confusion about the right of way, especially at roundabouts. Take particular care when crossing roads on foot, even where there is a signal allowing you to do so.

Be cautious driving on minor roads, particularly at night outside towns. Roads and vehicles may not have lighting.

In Algeria roads can have:
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Transport risks > Road conditions and safety

text:
Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Transport risks > Road conditions and safety — - sand drifts – slow down as you approach these
- large potholes, which can appear quickly, particularly after heavy rain
- large speed bumps

At military or police checkpoints, approach slowly, do not cross boundaries without permission and be prepared to show photo ID if asked.

Check the availability of petrol stations before travelling long distances in remote areas.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Transport risks > Road conditions and safety

text: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Transport risks > Taxis — If you are taking a taxi, ask your hotel to phone a reputable firm and do not allow unknown passengers to join you. Ask the driver to collect you for the return journey as taxis are not widely available, particularly after dark.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Transport risks > Taxis

text: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Transport risks > Rail travel — Rail travel is generally safe, although safety standards tend to be lower than those in the UK. There is a risk of petty crime on trains.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Transport risks > Rail travel

text: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Extreme weather and natural disasters — Find out what you can do to prepare for and respond to extreme weather and natural hazards.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Extreme weather and natural disasters

text: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Extreme weather and natural disasters > Wildfires — Wildfires take place most summers, causing significant damage and risk to life where they take place. Fires could flare up without warning, especially during periods of extreme weather. The General Directorate of Civil Contingency has released advice on how to help prevent wildfires and what to do if a wildfire breaks out near you. Always follow local advice and stay away from high risk areas.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Extreme weather and natural disasters > Wildfires

text: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Extreme weather and natural disasters > Flooding — Parts of Algeria are prone to severe and dangerous flood damage. There have been instances where people have been killed, houses submerged and cars swept away.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Extreme weather and natural disasters > Flooding

text:
Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Extreme weather and natural disasters > Earthquakes — Earthquakes are a risk in the northern part of Algeria, including Algiers.

In May 2003, a severe earthquake struck the Algiers area. There were over 2,200 dead and more than 10,000 injured. Smaller earthquakes happen regularly. In July 2014, an earthquake killed 6 people and injured 420.

The US Federal Emergency Management Agency website has advice about what to do before, during and after an earthquake.
heading_path: Safety and security — Algeria travel advice > Extreme weather and natural disasters > Earthquakes
